players.product: X-ray metrology for 3D transistor & advanced-packaging process control (with Onto AI Diffract)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (January - December 2025) results: revenue JPY 94,193 million, up 3.9% (JPY 90,652 million a year earlier); operating income JPY 16,709 million, down 9.0%; profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 11,401 million, down 16.3%. Adjusted operating income JPY 18,664 million (margin 19.8% vs 23.1%); adjusted EBITDA JPY 21,707 million (margin 23.0% vs 25.9%). Management states analytical-instrument demand returned to a growth path outside the US in the second half and AI / data-center demand kept driving the semiconductor market; capturing that demand gave a sharp Q4 sales increase year on year and quarter on quarter, recovering from negative growth through the first nine months to 3.9% growth for the year. It attributes the profit decline to the capacity expansion and continued strategic R&D, product / regional mix in semiconductor process control equipment, lower demand for high-margin EUV parts and lower US service sales hit by Trump-administration policies. No single customer accounted for 10% or more of sales.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue JPY 94,193 million (+3.9%); operating income JPY 16,709 million (-9.0%); adjusted operating margin 19.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor process control equipment (XRF / XRR / XRD in-line metrology) FY2025 revenue JPY 27,834 million, up 19.0% (JPY 23,391 million in FY2024); by destination Japan JPY 6,704 million, US JPY 7,288 million, Europe JPY 1,611 million, Asia JPY 12,230 million. Management states sales to semiconductor memory makers rose sharply on AI-driven DRAM and 3D NAND demand, as did sales to semiconductor equipment makers centred on next-generation technology development projects; because measurement demand shifted from mass-production to development purposes, sales and high-margin deals were concentrated in Q4, but the company was able to close them reliably.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor process control equipment revenue JPY 27,834 million (+19.0%)

quarterly_data.signal: Other product categories in FY2025: multi-purpose analytical instruments (XRD, XRF, X-ray CT) revenue JPY 40,413 million (JPY 41,327 million a year earlier), down 2.2%, on lower Americas and China sales - Trump-administration policies hit US academia and government demand, a China supplementary-budget boost from the prior first half fell away, and the EV-related SiC demand surge reversed globally - while Europe, Japan and other Asia grew strongly in Q4. Parts and services revenue JPY 25,945 million (JPY 25,934 million), flat: sales of EUV multilayer mirrors (a component Rigaku supplies to semiconductor equipment makers for EUV mask inspection tools) fell as customers' inventory adjustment dragged on, offset by growth in services and other analytical instruments.
quarterly_data.figure: Multi-purpose analytical instruments JPY 40,413 million (-2.2%); parts and services JPY 25,945 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 orders received JPY 88,861 million (110.1% of the prior year); order backlog at year-end JPY 26,727 million (82.7% of the prior year-end); production JPY 41,312 million at cost (116.8%).
quarterly_data.figure: Orders received JPY 88,861 million (110.1% y/y); order backlog JPY 26,727 million (82.7% y/y)

quarterly_data.signal: Market position the company states: citing Yole Group data, the global semiconductor X-ray metrology market was about US$498 million in 2024 and is expected to reach US$643 million in 2027 (an 8.9% annual average growth rate), and Rigaku was the market leader with a 38% share in 2024. Rigaku also states it does business with all of the top 10 companies by semiconductor capex and has a balanced revenue mix across memory, logic and power devices, which it says makes the business resilient to the silicon cycle. In X-ray diffraction (XRD) it held the No. 1 domestic share (76%, citing R&D Co.'s Scientific Instruments Yearbook 2025) and the No. 2 global share (26%, citing SDi's Global Assessment Report 2025) in 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: 38% share of the ~US$498 million (2024) semiconductor X-ray metrology market

quarterly_data.signal: Medium-term growth targets (company plan): semiconductor process control equipment revenue to grow about 18% a year on average, or more, versus 8.9% market growth (2024-2027), by gaining X-ray metrology share and expanding from X-ray metrology into optical and CD metrology; the company says optical and X-ray techniques complement each other in hybrid metrology and it is actively pursuing outside partnerships to deliver it. Multi-purpose analytical instruments revenue to grow about 7% a year on average, above the 4.6% XRD / XRF market growth, returning revenue and margins to an expansion trend after 2025, a plateau caused by the market cycle and US policy. The company also plans to enter the advanced-packaging inspection market: it is developing measurement technology and AI-based inspection algorithms for defect inspection of complex structures such as micro-bumps and TSVs in larger, 3D next-generation AI-chip packages, with productization under way for practical use in the near future.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor process control revenue growth ~18% a year or more; multi-purpose analytical instruments ~7% a year

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: Rigaku carried out a major expansion of its main plant, the Yamanashi plant, over 2024-2025, completing a new manufacturing building in May 2025; together with productivity measures and added production space at the Osaka plant and outside partners, the plan doubles group production capacity versus 2022 and contributed significantly to FY2025 results, and lets XRD manufacturing, assembly and shipping be consolidated from Tokyo into Yamanashi. The planned-facilities table lists the Yamanashi plant (Hokuto, Yamanashi) expansion at a total of JPY 5,314 million, JPY 4,577 million already paid, started June 2024, completion planned May 2026, raising product manufacturing capacity by 33.7%.
quarterly_data.figure: Yamanashi plant expansion JPY 5,314 million; +33.7% manufacturing capacity; completion May 2026

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 capex JPY 6,653 million (CAPEX ratio 7.1%), mainly the Yamanashi plant expansion, production equipment, demonstration equipment, equipment for joint development programs and an integrated HR system. R&D expenses JPY 7,355 million (R&D ratio 7.8%, up 0.3 points; R&D spending up 7.6%); the company states raising the R&D ratio is a management goal.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 6,653 million (7.1% of revenue); R&D JPY 7,355 million (7.8%)

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor metrology products from the FY2025 R&D results: XTRAIA XD-3300 micro-spot high-resolution XRD system entered full commercial production in July 2025 - it measures the Si/SiGe superlattice stacks used in HBM, 3D DRAM and 2nm-and-beyond logic non-destructively with high throughput. XHEMIS TX-3000 total-reflection XRF (TXRF) wafer-contamination analyzer went on sale in August 2025; Rigaku says its TXRF technology is the de facto industry standard, adoption at major semiconductor makers is expanding with this high-end model, and it expects this product segment to grow roughly double digits every year. XTRAIA MF-3400 in-line film thickness / composition tool (XRF, XRR and XRD) went on sale in December 2025, with about 2x the X-ray intensity and a new handling system that sharply raises wafers measured per hour; DRAM and logic makers are evaluating its adoption.
quarterly_data.figure: XD-3300 full production July 2025; TX-3000 on sale August 2025; MF-3400 on sale December 2025

quarterly_data.signal: ONYX 3200 semiconductor metrology tool went on sale in December 2025 for BEOL and packaging processes: it non-destructively measures metal layers thinner than a hair and micro-bumps of 10 micrometres or less, and measures the complex metal layers of a bump on one tool where several tools were used before. The first unit has already shipped to a foundry customer for its packaging process, and the company states it has many inquiries from leading semiconductor companies.
quarterly_data.figure: First ONYX 3200 shipped to a foundry customer's packaging line; bumps of 10 micrometres or less

quarterly_data.signal: Other FY2025 R&D results: the MoleQlyze solution-molecule projection system (electron density topography of proteins in solution, for biopharmaceuticals) delivered its first unit in August 2025 after a Boston demo lab opened in November 2024, with many inquiries from biopharma companies including mega-pharma; the Qualana micro-spot XRF analyzer (X-rays focused to as small as 20 micrometres) was announced in September 2025 with sales planned from spring 2026. The XRTmicron X-ray topography tool sells about 10 units a year as SiC power devices enter full use, and the XRTmicron Hybrid is more than 10x faster though at lower resolution, measuring a 6-inch wafer in 2-3 minutes, aimed at production lines as well as R&D.
quarterly_data.figure: XRTmicron about 10 units a year; MoleQlyze first unit August 2025
